## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world MMORPG-style game in the existing workspace.

## Requirements
- Procedural 5000×5000 world with 4 regions and 3D characters/buildings.
- Movable and rotatable character/camera, tutorial starter gear, combat, NPCs, monsters, quests, loot, shops, cosmetics, gacha, rarity tiers, dialogue choices, and branching endings.
- Include swordman, archer, mage, alchemy, assassin, and priest jobs.
- Weapon/armor rarities: copper, iron, gold, diamond, and adamantite.
- Main and side missions, currency, gacha tokens, varied loot, and 5 ending types.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js and Vite for the 3D browser game.
- Use procedural geometry and browser-generated audio to avoid external asset dependencies.
- Use localStorage for save data.
- Represent the world as one procedural 5000×5000 map divided into Verdant, Ember, Frost, and Umbral zones.
- Generate characters, monsters, buildings, props, and combat effects programmatically.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a Vite package setup with Three.js.
- Built the initial HTML title/game shell and extensive responsive visual CSS.
- Added game data for jobs, rarity levels, equipment, monsters, loot, NPCs, zones, cosmetics, potions, quests, and endings.
- Added procedural 3D model helpers for characters, monsters, buildings, shrines, settlements, props, and environmental objects.
- Implemented a procedural world generator with 4 regions, terrain, settlements, POIs, waypoints, NPC and monster spawns.
- Added procedural ambient audio and synthesized SFX.
- Added a core game controller module, combat module, skills module, quests module, dialogue module, and UI module.
- Added quest boards to settlements and HUD currency display.
- Added branching story/dialogue infrastructure and a system for five ending types.

### Active
- Integrating all modules into a working end-to-end game loop.
- Completing final wiring and runtime validation.

### Blocked
- Progress has not yet reached final browser verification or confirmation of a complete playable build.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and complete `src/main.js`, because it is the primary runtime controller and not fully described in the recovered work.
2. Resolve any module export/import mismatches and incomplete method integrations between `game.js`, `ui.js`, `combat.js`, `skills.js`, `quests.js`, and `dialogue.js`.
3. Run `npm install`, `npm run build`, and start the Vite server.
4. Capture and inspect a browser screenshot, fix rendering/runtime issues, and verify movement, combat, dialogue, shops, gacha, quests, save/load, and ending paths.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: Primary state, save/load, world interaction, tutorial, player state, and quest objective controller.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: 5000×5000 procedural terrain and regional POI/world generation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/models.js`: Procedural 3D characters, monsters, buildings, props, and model effects.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/combat.js`: Enemy spawning, monster AI/combat, drops, and boss defeat rewards.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/skills.js`: Class abilities and player skill behavior.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/quests.js`: Main and side quest generation, tracking, and rewards.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/dialogue.js`: NPC interactions and branching story dialogue.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: Menus, inventory, journal, gacha, map, dialogue, and modal interfaces.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: Procedural ambient audio and SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: Full responsive game visual and HUD styling.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world MMORPG-style game in the existing workspace.
- Finish end-to-end integration and validate gameplay in a browser.

## Requirements
- Procedural 5000×5000 world with four regions, 3D characters and buildings, movement, camera rotation, combat, NPCs, quests, loot, shops, cosmetics, gacha, dialogue choices, and branching endings.
- Include swordsman, archer, mage, alchemy, assassin, and priest jobs; copper, iron, gold, diamond, and adamantite equipment; currency, tokens, varied loot, and five ending types.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js and Vite, procedural geometry and browser-generated audio, and localStorage saves.
- Keep the world as one procedural map divided into Verdant, Ember, Frost, and Umbral zones.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `src/main.js` bootstrap wiring combat, skills, quests, dialogue, and UI prototype extensions onto `Game`.
- Implemented quest board, shop buy/sell, gacha, world map, fast travel, and minimap UI in `src/ui.js`; connected minimap drawing from `src/game.js`.
- Fixed `ReferenceError: sz is not defined` in `src/models.js`.
- `npm run build` succeeds. Vite dev server starts at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Browser boot and Embark were verified: game entered play mode with 137 enemies and 16 NPCs; movement changed player position and tutorial travel progress.
- Browser console had no errors after the building fix. Quest acceptance, gacha roll, and opening inventory, map, shop, board, and dialogue were exercised; these checks were partly invoked through game methods.

### Active
- Validate gameplay paths through normal player interactions, including combat, quest progression/rewards, shops, fast travel, save/load, dialogue branching, and endings.
- Review browser presentation and fix any remaining runtime or UI issues.

### Blocked
- No current blocker. Earlier browser verification was blocked by missing Chromium; Chromium was installed and browser testing proceeded.

## Next Move
1. Test combat, quest completion/rewards, purchases and sales, fast travel, save/load, dialogue choices, and ending selection in-browser.
2. Check for regressions and fix any remaining gameplay or UI issues.
3. Re-run `npm run build`; note that it currently emits a large-chunk warning for the 677 kB JavaScript bundle.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Runtime bootstrap and module integration.
- `src/game.js`: Game state, lifecycle, save/load, player and world interactions.
- `src/ui.js`: Modal interfaces, shops, quest board, gacha, map, fast travel, and minimap.
- `src/combat.js`: Enemy spawning, combat, drops, and boss rewards.
- `src/skills.js`: Class abilities and player attacks.
- `src/quests.js`: Quest generation, tracking, and rewards.
- `src/dialogue.js`: NPC dialogue, story branches, and ending choices.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural map, regions, settlements, NPCs, enemies, and waypoints.
- `src/models.js`: Procedural models; includes the `sz` fix.
- `src/data.js`: Jobs, equipment, monsters, quests, shops, and endings.
- `src/style.css`: Game and UI styling.
- `index.html`: Game shell and `src/main.js` entry point.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; the workspace contains untracked project files.
- Save key: `aetherfall_save_v1`.
- Browser tests included direct method calls for several interfaces; normal interaction paths and quest/dialogue/ending progression remain unverified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world MMORPG-style game in the existing workspace.
- Validate core gameplay and browser presentation end to end.

## Requirements
- Procedural 5000×5000 world with four regions; 3D characters and buildings; movement and camera rotation.
- Six jobs, five equipment rarities, tutorial starter gear, varied monsters and loot, NPC shops and stories, quests, cosmetics and gacha, and five dialogue-driven endings.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, Vite, procedural geometry, browser-generated audio, and localStorage saves.
- Represent the four regions as zones on one procedural map.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game bootstrap, combat and skills, quests and dialogue, shops, gacha, map and fast travel, minimap, and save/load integration.
- Fixed the `sz` reference error in `src/models.js` and duplicate “Copper” in starter armor naming in `src/data.js`.
- Improved mobile HUD/class selection, camera distance, and culling of distant enemies and NPCs.
- Browser-validated movement, combat and loot, side-quest acceptance/completion and rewards, shop purchase, waypoint travel, save/load, dialogue choices, and all five ending screens.
- `npm run build` succeeds; browser console showed no errors in tested paths.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optionally review the uncommitted changes and rerun `npm run build` before delivery.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Runtime bootstrap and module integration.
- `src/game.js`: Game state, lifecycle, save/load, movement, and interactions.
- `src/ui.js`: Modal interfaces, shops, quest board, gacha, map, and fast travel.
- `src/combat.js`: Enemy spawning, combat, and drops.
- `src/skills.js`: Job abilities and attacks.
- `src/quests.js`: Quest generation, tracking, and rewards.
- `src/dialogue.js`: Story branches and ending choices.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural map, regions, settlements, NPCs, enemies, and waypoints.
- `src/data.js`: Jobs, equipment, monsters, quests, shops, and endings.
- `src/style.css`: Game and responsive UI styling.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Save key: `aetherfall_save_v1`.
- Ending screens were tested by setting progression state directly; the full story was not played organically from start to finish.
- Production build reports a large JavaScript chunk (677.34 kB; 184.35 kB gzip) warning.
